Before MK2: Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa Built the Mortal Kombat Movie on His Shoulders

story // May 11, 2026 · Updated Sep 24, 2026

Watch on YouTube

As the world headed to theaters for Mortal Kombat II, I wanted to take a moment to honor the man who set the standard.

Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa died in December 2025, at 75. From the 1995 tournament to his final roles, he wasn't just an actor in a video game movie. He was the soul of the tournament.

This tribute has five chapters: the villain, the actor, the artist, the mentor and the angel.

The villain: Shang Tsung in Mortal Kombat (1995)

"Your soul is mine."

Nobody says it like him. The 1995 Mortal Kombat worked because Tagawa played Shang Tsung like he was in a real epic, not a video game movie. He was elegant, cruel and completely in control, and he looked like he was having the time of his life. A villain like that makes the heroes matter.

Years later, he came back to the role one more time, voicing Shang Tsung and lending him his likeness in the Mortal Kombat 11 video game.

The actor: The Man in the High Castle

A lot of people only knew him as Shang Tsung until The Man in the High Castle. In Amazon's alternate-history series, where the Axis powers won World War II, he played Nobusuke Tagomi, the Japanese Trade Minister in San Francisco: a quiet, thoughtful man trying to hold onto his conscience inside a brutal system. It's one of the best performances of his career.

The artist: Teen Titans: Trouble in Tokyo

In the 2006 movie Teen Titans: Trouble in Tokyo, Tagawa voiced Brushogun, an artist trapped inside a cursed printing press that uses his powers against his will to create criminals. It's a sad, strange role, and his voice gives it real weight.

The mentor: Johnny Tsunami

For a lot of Disney Channel kids, he was Johnny's grandfather, the surfing legend in Johnny Tsunami (1999). "I'm proud of you, son." Warm, funny and wise, and about as far from Shang Tsung as you can get. That's how much range he had.

The angel

The tribute ends with a digital art reveal in his honor. Rest in peace to a true legend.

Why he set the standard

Video game movies had a rough reputation in the '90s, and plenty of them earned it. Tagawa is a big reason Mortal Kombat is remembered differently. He took the role seriously, and that let the audience take it seriously too. Every Shang Tsung since has been measured against him.

Update (September 2026)

Mortal Kombat II opened on May 8 with about $38.5 million in the U.S. and finished around $129 million worldwide, on a reported $80 million budget.

Sources: Deadline, CNN, Wikipedia: Mortal Kombat II (film))

Quick answers

Who played Shang Tsung in the 1995 Mortal Kombat movie? Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa.

When did Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa die? On December 4, 2025, at 75, from complications of a stroke.

Who did Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa play in The Man in the High Castle? Nobusuke Tagomi, the Japanese Trade Minister.

Was Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa in Johnny Tsunami? Yes. He played Johnny's grandfather in the 1999 Disney Channel movie.

When did Mortal Kombat II come out? May 8, 2026.
